conventions.frame: CAD assembly frame: +Y up, robot front (OLED) faces -X, left = +Z, right = -Z
conventions.bind_pose: pose of the STEP export = firmware STAND pose; all geometry is stored in it
conventions.kinematics: app/kinematics.py: a joint rotates its link about the line through `pivot` along `axis` by sign * (angle - bind_angle) degrees (right-handed)
conventions.links: 'body' + one link per joint: R1/R2/L1/L2 = femurs (hip yaw), R3/L3/R4/L4 = feet (knee pitch; R3 on R1, L3 on L1, R4 on R2, L4 on L2)

screen.note: active 128x64 area of the 0.96in OLED, 0.05 mm proud of the display window block ('screen_glass'), centred in the cover's window opening; right = increasing pixel x for a viewer facing the robot, up = towards pixel row 0

mass.method: Rough estimate, default cover. Printed parts: exact B-rep volume x 0.87 g/cm3 (PLA 1.24 x ~0.7 fill). Servo bodies: 8.6 g each (SG90 = 9 g with horn and screws); horns: volume x POM 1.41; screws: volume x steel 7.9. Fixed guesses: battery 40 g (2x 14500), distro PCB incl. unmodelled MCU board and wiring 12 g, OLED module 3 g, switch 3 g. COMs are B-rep centres of mass in the bind pose.

buffers.indices: uint32 (T,3), relative to the part's vertex_offset
